title: Bílá rybí polévka (Fish Soup, White)
description: A soup made with fish, celery, and leek or onion.

ingredients.name: four whole eggs and two egg yolks
ingredients.sourceText: four whole eggs and two egg yolks

steps: Put several pieces of various fish in a pan
add celery, parsley, leek or white onion and let it stew
then fry several pieces of bread
crush it in a mortar with hard-boiled egg yolks
put this with the stewed mixture in a pot
pour fish bouillon on it and let it boil
meanwhile beat four whole eggs and two egg yolks into a small cup of cold clear fish soup
add a little flowers to it
beat well, cover with clean cloth, tie the cup with string
hang it in boiling water and let it boil for one hour
then take it out with a small spoon into a bowl like small dumplings
strain the soup, beat it with several egg yolks
add flowers to it, and if you have it, a little crayfish butter
pour it into a bowl over the dumplings

title: Bílé Mandle Cukrové (White Sugared Almonds)
description: Prepared with almonds and sugar.
steps: Select fine large almonds and rub with cloth to remove all dust
Place in a pot or saucepan
Boil fine refined sugar
Continuously stir almonds in the container so they heat evenly over the heat
Add crushed sugar and continue stirring until each almond is coated
When dry, add new sugar and repeat several times until a complete sugar layer forms around the almonds
Finally, pour melted warm sugar to give the almonds shine
Remove almonds from container several times and place on a sieve to collect debris and fine sugar
Crush and melt this sugar again, then pour warm back onto the almonds

title: Chlebové Hůlčičky (Bread Sticks)
description: A bread preparation made with bread dough, dough, and lard.

ingredients.name: about 1 pound or 1 large quart of dough
ingredients.sourceText: about 1 pound or 1 large quart of dough

steps: When making bread with liquid yeast, after the dough made from sourdough is rolled out and worked, take a piece of dough according to how many sticks you want.
For a piece of dough about 1 pound or 1 large quart in size, take 1 tablespoon of lard and work it in well and let it rise.
When risen, take it to the work surface, roll it a little and then cut into pieces which you roll into long sticks.
In the meantime, grease the grooves in the pan with lard, place the rolled sticks into them and let them rise for three quarters of an hour in a warm place.
Before putting them in the oven, make a nice hot fire so that the oven is nicely hot at the bottom, which is necessary for the iron pan to heat properly.
If needed, cover the top of the pan with paper.
Bake for about 25 minutes and when nicely baked golden, place on a plate.
They taste best when warm, like biscuits, but when they cool down, they are also eaten.

title: Dušená kuřátka s kyselou omáčkou (Stewed Chicken with Sour Cream Gravy)

Place the stewed chicken in this sauce and let it cook a bit.
Before serving, beat two egg yolks with a little sour cream, mix it into the sauce, place the chicken on a platter, strain the sauce over it, and serve.
If desired, you can squeeze lemon juice into it.

ingredients.name: beef from the hindquarters

steps: Pound about {{source-0}} well with a wooden mallet, put it in a pot, pour a little wine vinegar over it and let it marinate thus for about twenty-four hours.

When you then want to prepare the meat, lard it with bacon cut into thick strips, put it in a pot, salt it, add a little vinegar, a little meat beef broth, one sliced onion, a piece of carrot, bay leaf, several peppercorns, new spice, clove, cover it and let it stew slowly until tender.
Meanwhile melt one heaping spoon of butter in another pan, put one spoon of flour and one spoon of sugar in it and brown it to make a roux.

To this gradually pour in about two cups of beef broth, from which you have skimmed off all fat, or hot water if you do not have broth, and the sauce from the stewed meat, from which you have also skimmed off all fat.
Let it boil about a quarter hour until you have from it a thick, brown, pleasantly sour sauce.
When you have skimmed off any additional fat, pour the sauce over the stewed meat and let it boil a little more.
Then place the meat on a plate, pour part of the sauce over it, bring to the table and serve the rest of the sauce in a separate bowl.
You can also add fried potatoes or dumplings to this.

steps: Pound {{source-0}} with a wooden mallet and slice it into cutlets, about a finger thick, pound again.
Sprinkle them then with salt, a little all-spice and a little flour, lay bacon thinly sliced on the cutlets, roll up each cutlet, fasten with a skewer and coat in flour.

Melt a piece of fresh butter in a pot, dip the rolled cutlets in it, lay them next to each other in the pot, cover and let the cutlets fry about ten minutes on moderate heat, during which time you must turn them once.
Then add to the cutlets from the side as much boiling water until they are submerged halfway, but watch that they do not get wet on the surface.
Then cover the pot so that the lid fits completely and let the beef rolls simmer on moderate heat for an hour.
Then put the rolls on a plate, remove the skewers from them, arrange fried potatoes around them and add the sauce.

title: Edamský sýr (Edam Cheese)
description: Prepared with rennet, milk, and salt.
steps: Uncollected, freshly milked milk is strained into a vessel, kept warm, and curdled with the help of rennet.
The cheese is broken several times in succession, then the vessel is covered and allowed to stand quietly for about a quarter hour, then the cheese is removed and the whey is poured off.
The cheese is allowed to settle, is mixed, and is pressed into curds; when it hardens, it is removed and crumbled again.
Cheese molds are soaked in whey, cheese is firmly pressed into them to expel the whey.
The cheese removed from the molds is crumbled and crumbled again and placed into molds again, which is repeated several times until the cheese hardens completely.
In the molds the cheese is often flipped, pressed, then placed into smaller molds, salted, flipped, and turned.
In a few weeks the cheese matures and is very tasty.

steps: Remove all glands and fat from one and a half pounds of boiled beef and chop the meat finely.
Make a pale roux from butter and flour, then pour enough beef broth into it to make a thick sauce, then let it, stirring constantly, boil for a quarter hour.
Then mix in a cup a piece of butter with three egg yolks, add this mixture to the sauce, which you then stir well.
To this add the mentioned chopped meat, one spoon of cleaned and finely chopped parsley leaves, a little ground pepper, salt it and mix well with a spoon.

Then let it cool completely, sprinkle generously with grated stale bread, bread crumbs or crackers; then divide the prepared meat into 16 portions, and place each portion on a layer of this grated bread spread on a board, then again sprinkle generously with grated bread crumbs, from this make equally large and oblong rolls.
Then beat 3 egg whites, add to them {{source-10}}, one teaspoon of water and mix well.

Dip each roll in this and coat it in grated bread crumbs; then about 20 minutes before you want to put the rolls on the table, melt lard in a pot, place the rolls on a wire basket (frying basket) and hang this in the pot in the heated lard and let them fry.
Then turn them with a spoon and let them fry nicely to golden brown, then remove, sprinkle with salt, arrange on a plate, surround with fried parsley and bring them to the table.

title: Hroznový rosol (Grape Jelly)
description: Prepared with grape, water, and sugar.
steps: Remove the grains from unripened grapes and put in a pot or kettle

For every 8 pounds of grapes (a small basket of grapes holds 8 pounds, a large one 20 pounds) add 1 small cup of water and let it cook about 1/2 hour until the grains are completely cooked, stirring occasionally so the skins do not stick to the bottom
When cooked, set aside and let cool
Then strain through thin cloth (cheese cloth)
If you want clear jelly, let it only drip and do not squeeze much
Measure the juice and pour it back into the pot and for however many small cups of juice, prepare that many small cups of fine sugar

Put the sugar in the oven to warm, but do not let it burn and when the juice has cooked 1/2 hour, add the sugar to it, let it cook another 10 minutes, during which collect the foam, then set aside and when it cools, put in jars
Jelly from wild grape is also very delicious

steps: Sort the peas the evening before, wash them thoroughly in cold water and let them soak in it overnight.
For cooking, take an elongated (tall) but not large pot.
Peas nearly double in volume when cooked, so if you want to cook about two small cups of peas, take a quart pot.
Drain the water in which the peas soaked and put the peas in the pot and add soft cold water until the pot is full.
If you do not have soft water, add a pinch of soda to it.
Cover and as the water boils away, replenish with hot water and when it has boiled away, salt it.

steps: Boil the goose giblets.
When they float, add a piece of celery and parsley root, salt them, and cook until tender.
On a stove put three tablespoons of fresh butter and one cup of sifted rice that has been rinsed several times in hot water.
Pour a few tablespoons of beef broth over it, salt lightly, and let the rice stew slowly on low heat until tender.
Watch carefully so it does not stick to the bottom and add more beef broth as needed.
Make a light roux and thin it with a little beef broth, season with nutmeg, salt, and let it cook into a smooth sauce.
Finally arrange the cooked goose giblets on a serving dish, pour the sauce over them, make a wreath of rice around them, and place diagonal strips of finely chopped smoked meat on top.
Instead of roux, you can also use drippings from the roast or fry a little caraway seed in butter or goose fat, to which add a little chopped fresh parsley.
Do not forget to add a little nutmeg and a small amount of saffron to the rice.
The giblets include wings, legs, neck, liver, and stomach. Well-cleaned intestines, when turned inside out, can also be used and serve as a good delicacy.

Do not forget to add a little nutmeg and a small amount of saffron to the rice.
The giblets include wings, legs, neck, liver, and stomach. Well-cleaned intestines, when turned inside out, can also be used and serve as a good delicacy.

title: Husí Drobečky Zadělávané s Nudlemi (Goose Giblets with Noodles)
description: Prepared with goose, carrots, and celery.
steps: Clean the giblets, especially the stomach, cut them up, and place in water
Add carrots, celery, parsley, cabbage, cauliflower, and salt; cook until completely soft
Allow to cool
Make thin noodles from one or two eggs
Strain the broth in which the giblets were cooked onto a separate baking pan
Add a piece of white roux, strain it, and cook the noodles in the boiling broth
For a sour taste, add lemon juice
Peel the stomach and cut into small pieces, then add with the remaining giblets to the sauce

title: Husí Drůbky s Rejží (Goose Giblets with Rice)
description: Prepared with goose, rice, and carrots.
steps: Prepare the giblets as when preparing them with noodles
When they have cooked for about half an hour, rinse the rice and place on a separate baking pan
Pour about two spoonfuls of broth from the giblets gradually until the rice is completely soft
When both are soft, add a little cauliflower and mix the giblets with the rice
